content: As observed from Table TABREF44, ALOHA performs slightly better overall compared to ALOHA (No HLA-OG). Table TABREF45 shows that this slight performance increase is consistent across four of the five evaluation characters. In the case of Sheldon, the HLA-OG model performs a bit worse. This is possibly due to the large number of Sheldon's HLAs (217) compared to the other four evaluation characters (average of 93.75), along with the limited amount of HLAs we are using for guidance due to the models' limited memory. In general, HLA Observation Guidance during testing appears to improve upon the performance of ALOHA, but this improvement is minimal.
